title: Rental assistance can improve immediate rent payment and eviction anxiety without producing large measured housing-stability effects
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 32463, revised October 2025, evaluating five emergency rental-assistance programs in four U.S. cities using lottery assignment, administrative data, and surveys
geography: Four U.S. cities and five pandemic-era emergency rental-assistance programs distributing more than $200 million; applicant and recipient households in program-specific lottery samples

observations.period: Pandemic-era emergency rental assistance programs; five lotteries in four cities

denominator.unit: rental-assistance programs evaluated through embedded lotteries

funding_scale.unit: assistance distributed by the evaluated programs

data.value: administrative and survey data on rent payment, housing stability, financial distress, and health

observations.method: Evaluation using embedded program lotteries, administrative records, and follow-up surveys; the paper compares recipients and lottery-based nonrecipients within program-specific designs.
observations.uncertainty: Programs, timing, local markets, and pandemic-era policy conditions differ across cities; the pooled description does not imply one identical treatment or a universal effect.
observations.subgroup: Low-income renter applicants to five emergency rental-assistance programs in four cities; applicants not represented in the lotteries are outside the experimental comparison.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lottery-based access identifies the effect of receiving assistance in these programs, but broader safety-net changes, eviction moratoria, and market conditions can affect measured housing outcomes.

denominator.unit: applicants in study-specific lottery samples; exact pooled denominator not used in this bounded extraction

mental_physical_health.value: suggestive improvements in self-reported mental and physical health

observations.method: Lottery-based comparison using administrative rent-payment measures and survey-reported concerns and health outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The health results are described as suggestive and self-reported; the extraction does not convert them into clinical outcomes or durable wellbeing.
observations.subgroup: Lottery applicants who received or did not receive assistance in the evaluated programs.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reduced anxiety or improved rent payment may be valuable even if housing tenure does not change; effects can differ across program design and pandemic conditions.

observations.period: Pandemic-era comparison with pre-pandemic emergency rental assistance

denominator.unit: study comparison across evaluated pandemic programs and prior evidence; no common household panel denominator

possible_explanations.value: eviction moratoria, expanded safety-net programs, and tenant-favoring market conditions weakened the link between rent and displacement

observations.method: Study authors' comparison of pandemic-era results with pre-pandemic emergency-rental-assistance evidence; explanations are not treated as separately identified causal effects.
observations.uncertainty: A small measured housing-stability effect does not prove assistance was ineffective; it may reflect reduced baseline displacement risk or other concurrent protections.
observations.subgroup: Pandemic-era applicants and comparison evidence from earlier rental-assistance settings.
observations.counterinterpretation: The intervention may have prevented rent arrears or distress without changing the observed housing-status measure; housing stability can be an insensitive endpoint over the follow-up window.

related_sources.claim: J-PAL's evaluation summary reports short-term rent-payment and modest mental-health effects from the lottery-based programs.

boundary: This record shows a bounded intervention effect: emergency rental assistance improved rent payment and reduced eviction concerns in evaluated pandemic programs, while large housing-stability or financial-distress effects were not detected. It does not establish national prevention of eviction, durable housing security, or a general failure of rental assistance.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: NBER revised working-paper PDF used for the extracted findings; lottery microdata and full replication are not locally reproduced.
